t: If C,R,L and I denote Capacitance, resistance, inductance and electric current respectively, the quantities having the same dimensions of time are : (1) CR (2) L/R (3) √LC (4) LI²

t: The position of a particle at time t is given by the equation x(t)=v₀/A(1−eᴬᵗ)vₒ= constant and A>0. Dimensions of vₒ and A respectively are
s:
In the given equation x(t)=v₀/A(1−eᴬᵗ), the exponent At must be a dimensionless quantity.
Therefore, the dimensional formula of At is [M⁰L⁰T⁰].
[A][T]=[M⁰L⁰T⁰]
[A]=[T⁻¹]=[M⁰L⁰T⁻¹]
The entire term (1−eᴬᵗ) is also dimensionless.
By the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, the dimensions of the position x(t) must be equal to the dimensions of v₀/A.
[x]=([v₀])/([A])
Substituting the dimensions of x and A:
[L]=([v₀])/([T⁻¹])
[v₀]=[L][T⁻¹]=[M⁰LT⁻¹]
Thus, the dimensions of v₀ and A are [M⁰LT⁻¹] and [M⁰L⁰T⁻¹] respectively.

t: A spherical body of mass m and radius r is allowed to fall in a medium of viscosity η. The time in which the velocity of the body increases from zero to 0.63 times the terminal velocity (v) is called time constant (τ). Dimensionally, τ can be represented by
s:
Equation of motion for a sphere falling in viscous medium:
mdv/dt=W_(eff)−6πηrv
Rearranging: dv/dt+(6πηr/m)v=(W_(eff))/m
This is of the form dv/dt+v/τ=constant, giving solution v(t)=vₜ(1−e^(−t/τ))
The time constant τ is the reciprocal of the coefficient of v:
τ=m/6πηr
Correct option: (3) !

t: In the relation P=α/βe^(−αz/Kθ), P is pressure, z is distance, K is the Boltzmann constant, and θ is temperature. If the dimensional formula of β is [MˣLʸTᶻ], then what is the value of x+y+z?

Given: P=α/β e^(−αz/Kθ), where K is Boltzmann constant, θ is temperature, z is distance.
The exponent αz/Kθ must be dimensionless:
[α]=([Kθ])/([z])=([ML²T⁻²])/([L])=[MLT⁻²]
Since the exponential is dimensionless, [P]=([α])/([β]):
[β]=([α])/([P])=([MLT⁻²])/([ML⁻¹T⁻²])=[M⁰L²T⁰]
Given [β]=[MˣLʸTᶻ], comparing:
x=0, y=2, z=0
